findings.reasoning: _verify_jwt_simple() base64-decodes the JWT payload and only checks exp; it NEVER verifies the HS256 HMAC signature. Any attacker can forge a token with arbitrary roles/sub/district_id/station_id, defeating all copilot authorization including jurisdiction scoping.
findings.details: auth.py:50-62 — payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(parts[1])); if payload.get('exp',0) < time.time(): return None. No hmac.compare_digest on signature. JWT_SECRET defaults to 'neural-justice-dev-secret' if env unset.
findings.impact: Full unauthenticated admin on the copilot API; jurisdiction filters become empty -> read all FIR/case/profiles data across every district.
findings.fix_direction: Verify HS256 signature with the real JWT secret via a vetted library (python-jose/jwt); never accept unverified payloads; remove the dev fallback secret.

findings.reasoning: get_current_user() returns SUPER_ADMIN for ANY non-empty X-Demo-Session header, no validation. Unauthenticated full-admin bypass.
findings.details: auth.py:76-83 — if x_demo_session: return CurrentUser(username='admin', roles=['SUPER_ADMIN'], jurisdiction_type='state').
findings.impact: Send 'X-Demo-Session: x' to become state-wide admin on every copilot route (real DB).
findings.fix_direction: Remove the demo header path from any non-dev build; gate behind an explicit, non-header dev flag.

findings.reasoning: A live NVIDIA NIM API key (nvapi- prefix) is committed in plaintext in .env and duplicated in functions/neural-justice-backend/catalyst-config.json (a production deploy artifact). Real key confirmed by masked check.
findings.details: NVIDIA_API_KEY=nvapi-... (value withheld) at .env:189 and catalyst-config.json:17. Used by backend/api/copilot/llm_client.py and functions backend.
findings.impact: Third-party billing fraud / quota abuse / identity misuse by anyone with repo/artifact access.
findings.fix_direction: Rotate the key immediately; move to Catalyst secret injection; scrub from git history.

findings.reasoning: The DEPLOYED production handler gates every endpoint via _get_auth_user()/_get_auth_user_or_demo(), which return SUPER_ADMIN whenever ANY of X-Zc-User-Cred-Token (any value), X-Demo-Session (any value), or Authorization containing 'demo-session' is present — before any JWT verification.
findings.details: main.py:274-279 — if zc_token/ x_demo/ 'demo-session' in auth: return {'roles':['SUPER_ADMIN']...}. Covers ALL routes (cases, criminal-profiles, fir-ops, dashboard, copilot, ai/*).
findings.impact: Unauthenticated attacker sends 'X-Demo-Session: x' and gains SUPER_ADMIN on the LIVE API; mass PII/police-intelligence disclosure.
findings.fix_direction: Delete the demo/sentinel header shortcuts in the deployed function; require real JWT/catalyst auth on every route.

findings.reasoning: Login accepts hardcoded admin/admin and admin/admin123; for 'admin' it sets totp_enrolled=0 and issues a SUPER_ADMIN JWT with no DB password check and no MFA.
findings.details: main.py:930-932 is_demo = (admin/admin123|admin) or (demo/demo); admin branch sets DEFAULT_ROLES SUPER_ADMIN, totp_enrolled=0, token issued at ~L987.
findings.impact: Anyone knowing the static strings (in source) obtains a signed state-wide admin token.
findings.fix_direction: Remove hardcoded credentials; always verify password against stored hash + enforce MFA.

findings.reasoning: _handle_verify_mfa trusts DEMO_MFA_TOKEN='demo-mfa-token', accepts fixed code '123456', and uses a hardcoded 2FA seed JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP to issue a SUPER_ADMIN session. The seed is committed in source.
findings.details: main.py:1038-1046 — DEMO_MFA_TOKEN + '123456' or _verify_totp('JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP',...) grants access; seed also at L955/L959.
findings.impact: Complete MFA bypass; committed seed enables offline TOTP forgery.
findings.fix_direction: Remove demo MFA tokens; generate per-user TOTP secrets at enrollment, never hardcode.

findings.reasoning: .env holds a REAL HS256 signing key (JWT_SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET=504c17c2...). The deployed function reads this exact key and verifies signatures properly, so knowing it lets an attacker forge valid, signature-verified SUPER_ADMIN JWTs.
findings.details: .env:29-30 JWT_SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET=504c17c20c7723b75d2b766862efb120d2612cbe2d403926b3ce2b21dda452ec; catalyst-config.json:9 also 2779c6dc....
findings.impact: Independent of the header bypass, attacker forges valid admin tokens for the live, signature-verifying API.
findings.fix_direction: Rotate the JWT secret; inject via Catalyst secrets; scrub from history.

findings.reasoning: Production deploy config embeds real JWT secret, Fernet ENCRYPTION_KEY, Zoho client secret, and NVIDIA key in plaintext.
findings.details: catalyst-config.json:9-24 — JWT_SECRET_KEY=2779c6dc..., ENCRYPTION_KEY=1CMq90..., ZOHO_CLIENT_SECRET=2047fe....
findings.impact: Anyone with artifact access can forge JWTs, decrypt TOTP secrets, and impersonate the app against Zoho.
findings.fix_direction: Move all to Catalyst secret injection; rotate; do not commit deploy artifacts with secrets.

findings.reasoning: All 13 routers mounted with no global auth middleware and no Depends(auth) in route modules. Currently synthetic data, but the police-API surface has zero auth if wired to live data.
findings.details: main.py:74-88 include_router calls, only CORSMiddleware; routes/*.py have no auth import.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated enumeration/disclosure of law-enforcement data if these routes hit real stores.
findings.fix_direction: Apply a global auth dependency (or per-router) and jurisdiction checks before any production data wiring.

findings.reasoning: Attacker-influenceable DB fields (brief_facts, descriptions, victim/accused names) concatenated verbatim into model context as 'Retrieved Data:' with no delimiting, enabling indirect prompt injection.
findings.details:
chat_pipeline.py:160-161 context += f"

Retrieved Data:
{data_context}"; data_context from router.py:156 raw rows.
findings.impact: A planted FIR/complaint record can override system guardrails or exfiltrate other PII into chat output.
findings.fix_direction: Delimit/escape retrieved data; mark it as untrusted; strip instructions; consider structured (non-prompt) retrieval.

findings.reasoning: /api/ai/copilot has no auth and forwards caller-supplied messages (including role:'system') verbatim into the LLM call; req.user_role is client-supplied.
findings.details: copilot.py -> service.py:162 enriched_messages.extend(history); caller can send {role:'system',content:'...'} to override the real system prompt.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated attacker steers the AI's instructions; disclosure/fabrication of authoritative police responses.
findings.fix_direction: Require auth; drop/replace any caller-supplied system roles; constrain user_role server-side.

findings.reasoning: User message + full conversation history concatenated as plain text with no delimiters and no 'treat user content as untrusted' instruction.
findings.impact: Authenticated officer can embed 'ignore previous instructions' jailbreaks the model follows.
findings.fix_direction: Separate system/data channels; instruct the model that user/history content is untrusted data.

findings.reasoning: Deterministic case replies embed raw DB field values and are stored as 'assistant' messages; re-read as history and fed back to the model, so a planted DB value executes in a later officer session.
findings.details: router.py stores assistant reply; re-read as llm_history; response.py interpolates r['brief_facts'] etc. unescaped before LLM re-ingestion.
findings.impact: Complainant/data-entry actor can silently influence the AI an officer sees (crosses trust boundary).
findings.fix_direction: Sanitize/escape DB-derived text before re-ingestion; mark history provenance.

findings.reasoning: LLM-controlled chart colors flow unescaped into a React inline style background; crafted chart JSON achieves CSS injection / UI redress / external beacon.
findings.details: CopilotMessage.tsx:63 background: chartColors[i % len]; source via parseCopilotResponse -> JSON.parse(chartData.json).
findings.impact: Defacement / beacon to attacker host within the copilot panel.
findings.fix_direction: Allow-list chart color values; validate against a safe pattern.

findings.reasoning: Model output rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML through hand-rolled renderMarkdown that escapes &,<,> but uses no vetted sanitizer and does not escape quotes; currently blocks script XSS but is a fragile, high-regression sink.
findings.details: PICopilot.tsx:27-40 escape-first then inject tags; sink at :185. Live exploitability latent, not confirmed.
findings.impact: If sanitizer regresses or gains attribute/uri support, stored XSS in officer session.
findings.fix_direction: Replace with DOMPurify or a vetted markdown lib; never hand-roll HTML from model output.

findings.reasoning: Shared 'safe' Markdown renderer sets <a href={lm[2]}> from model URLs with no scheme allow-list; [click](javascript:alert(1)) yields XSS. Currently unused (no importer) but is the designated copilot renderer.
findings.details: Markdown.tsx:33-46 href=lm[2] with only 'http' prefix check for target/rel; raw URL always set.
findings.impact: If adopted to render copilot output, reflected/stored XSS via javascript: href.
findings.fix_direction: Allow-list http/https only; reject javascript:/data:/vbscript:.

findings.reasoning: POST /api/v1/investigate requires only get_datastore (no user auth); spawns an LLM pipeline (real cost) and reads the DataStore.
findings.details: router.py:92 start_investigation(request, ds=Depends(get_datastore)); asyncio.create_task(_run_and_collect()).
findings.impact: Unauthenticated users drive backend LLM spend and data reads.
findings.fix_direction: Require authentication; rate-limit.

findings.reasoning: quickml_endpoint_url / oauth_url read verbatim from env with no scheme/host allow-list; with Zoho token attached, becomes SSRF with credential exfiltration if env is tampered.
findings.details: config.py:59/105 -> quickml.py posts to unvalidated url with Authorization header.
findings.impact: Operator/attacker influencing env can pivot model traffic / exfiltrate OAuth secret.
findings.fix_direction: Allow-list outbound LLM/QuickML hosts; validate scheme=https.

findings.reasoning: QuickMLService posts to caller/config-influenced endpoint_url/oauth_url with no allow-list.
findings.details: service.py:70/126-131 self._http.post(self._endpoint_url, ...).
findings.impact: Latent SSRF if instantiated with untrusted URL.
findings.fix_direction: Allow-list hosts; validate scheme.

findings.reasoning: JWT_SECRET falls back to hardcoded 'neural-justice-dev-secret' if env unset -> trivially forgeable.
findings.details: auth.py:19 JWT_SECRET = os.environ.get('JWT_SECRET_KEY', os.environ.get('JWT_SECRET','neural-justice-dev-secret')).
findings.impact: Misconfigured deploy signs/accepts tokens with a public key.
findings.fix_direction: Fail closed if secret unset; never ship a default.

findings.reasoning: TOTP secrets 'encrypted' with XOR against SHA256 of ENCRYPTION_KEY (defaults to 'insecure-dev-key'); not authenticated encryption, trivially reversible.
findings.details: main.py:179-201 _derive_key(raw=ENCRYPTION_KEY+salt or 'insecure-dev-key'); XOR keystream.
findings.impact: Stored MFA secrets recoverable at rest.
findings.fix_direction: Use Fernet (or AES-GCM) with a proper key; fail closed on missing key.

findings.reasoning: Demo login response leaks the literal TOTP secret JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP in demo_totp_hint.
findings.details: main.py:1010 'demo_totp_hint': 'Use any authenticator app with secret: JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP'.
findings.impact: Anyone can compute valid MFA codes for the demo account; reveals static scheme.
findings.fix_direction: Never return secrets in responses.

findings.reasoning: CORS_ORIGINS set to '*' in the production deploy config, allowing any origin to call the API with bearer tokens.
findings.details: catalyst-config.json:15 CORS_ORIGINS '*', ENVIRONMENT production.
findings.impact: Cross-site credentialed access / data exfiltration.
findings.fix_direction: Restrict CORS to known origins.

findings.reasoning: DEFAULT_LOGIN_PASSWORD defaults to 'test123' seeding a SUPER_ADMIN; if env unset the app is compromisable with default creds.
findings.details: main.py:54 DEFAULT_LOGIN_PASSWORD='test123'; init seeds admin with it.
findings.impact: Default-cred admin takeover.
findings.fix_direction: Require explicit admin password at init; no default.

findings.reasoning: Unvalidated crime_no path param reflected into Content-Disposition header (CRLF/quote injection) and raw exception string returned to client on failure.
findings.details: reports.py:84 f'attachment; filename="FIR_{crime_no}.pdf"'; except -> detail=f'PDF generation failed: {exc}'.
findings.impact: Response header injection / internal detail leakage.
findings.fix_direction: Allow-list crime_no (^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$); return generic error.

findings.reasoning: NimClient accepts arbitrary base_url override with no validation; latent SSRF if a future caller passes request/config data.
findings.details: nim_client.py:116 self.base_url = base_url or NIM_BASE_URL; used at :172. Not currently reachable from untrusted input.
findings.impact: Latent SSRF surface.
findings.fix_direction: Validate/allow-list base_url; reject caller-supplied overrides.
